title: Chicken and Leek Pie
subtitle: Creamy chicken and leek filling under a rough pastry lid
excerpt: A proper British pie with chunks of chicken thigh and sweet leek in a creamy mustard sauce, topped with a rough shortcrust pastry lid. The pastry is made by rubbing butter into flour and does not need to be perfect to work well. It freezes before baking and comes out of the oven golden and ready.
sourceNotes: Based on the British chicken and leek pie tradition, with a homemade rough shortcrust lid.

recipe.freezeNotes: Assemble and freeze before baking. Bake from frozen at 190C for 50 to 55 minutes until golden.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling can be made 2 days ahead and kept in the fridge. Assemble and bake when needed.

content.text: For the rough pastry lid, the butter needs to be cold and cut into small cubes before rubbing into the flour. Overworking the pastry makes it tough; stop as soon as it comes together into a dough. You only need to roll it out to fit the top of the pie dish, so it can be a little uneven at the edges.

items.prepNote: cold and cut into small cubes

content.text: Make the pastry: put the self-raising flour in a bowl, add the cold salted butter cubes, and rub together with your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Add 3 to 4 tablespoons of cold water and bring together into a dough. Do not overwork. Wrap and rest in the fridge while you make the filling.
Season the chicken chunks and fry in a dry large saucepan over a medium-high heat for 5 minutes until lightly browned. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, melt the unsalted butter over a medium heat. Add the leek and thyme leaves and soften for 5 minutes.
Stir in the plain flour and cook for 2 minutes. Gradually pour in the chicken stock, whisking to avoid lumps.
Add the double cream and mustard. Simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens. Return the chicken and season well. Allow to cool slightly.
Preheat the oven to 190C. Pour the filling into a 20cm pie dish or deep baking dish.
Roll out the pastry on a lightly floured surface to roughly the size of the dish. Lay it over the filling and press the edges down. Score the top a couple of times to let steam out.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges.

items.cause: Overworked or too much water added
items.fix: Mix just until it comes together; stop before it looks smooth.

items.symptom: Filling is too runny under the pastry
items.cause: Sauce not thick enough before baking
items.fix: Simmer sauce longer until it coats the back of a spoon.
